8 places from one video about the most dangerous places in nature. From each I check one number. It checks out confirmed. Fine print inexact. The source says otherwise, wrong. How many of the 8 numbers hold up? We start with Danakil.

This is Erta Ale, a lava lake in Ethiopia. The video shows yellow, green, and rust-colored patches on the ground. And this is the whole depression, seen from a satellite. The video says, up to 55 degrees Celsius on hot days. Wikipedia, the highest recorded temperature is 49. The title for the highest average, for Dalol, is real. 34.6, but from the 1960s. Verdict inexact. My read, it is a record for the average, not for a day.

The Suedirkus wreck on the Skeleton Coast. In the video, waves pound a wreck. The wreck of the Eduard Bolin off Namibia's coast. The National Park page, about 500 kilometers. Wikipedia, 310 miles. Only Huffpost gives 976 miles. That is over 1500 kilometers. The story of the Dynedon star does check out. Verdict inexact. My read, a number without the coast's limits means nothing.

This is Senabung during an eruption. In the video at this point, you see a snowy slope. On the 1st of February, 2014, 16 people died. That checks out. But the eruption caught villagers returning home. The video, over 9,000 displaced. Earth sky in February, 2014, over 30,000. Verdict inexact. My read, the video simplified the story of those 16 people.

The summit of Everest in 2017. Wikipedia, at the summit, oxygen pressure is less than a third. The death zone starts at 8,000 meters. A view of Everest from the village of Siangaboche. The video also gives minus 120 degrees Fahrenheit and minus 49 Celsius. But minus 120 is minus 84. Verdict wrong. My read. In one sentence, the video contradicts itself.

Maheno, a shipwreck on the island's beach. In the video, you see a dune above a forest and shallows. A dingo on Fraser Island. The video warns of currents, sharks and jellyfish. Intrepid, powerful rips that pull even the strongest swimmers out. The Queensland government, Urukandji jellyfish, especially in summer. The only things I did not find in the sources, great whites and box jellyfish. Verdict confirmed. My read, an honest warning.
